target.title: fix(cli): bound media input file reads with per-file and aggregate budget
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readInputFiles` in `src/cli/capability-cli/media-output.ts` reads user-provided `--file` CLI argument files concurrently via `Promise.all` with no size limit. A user passing multiple large files to `openclaw image|document` capability commands would OOM the process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Unbounded `fs.readFile` on user-controlled paths is a known OOM vector. CLI input files (images, documents) should be reasonable — multi-GB files are not legitimate inputs for capability commands. Concurrent reads multiply the memory risk.

## What Changed

Replaced the `Promise.all` concurrent read pattern with sequential processing and an aggregate byte budget:

- **Per-file cap**: 100 MiB (statSync pre-check before read)
- **Command-wide budget**: 500 MiB tracked via a mutable accumulator
- Files are processed one at a time, with remaining budget checked before each read
- Exceeding either cap produces a clear error message

## Evidence

**All 109 capability CLI tests pass:**

```
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.10 /home/0668000387/openclawCxbAsDev

 ✓ |cli| src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts (109 tests) 2679ms
     ✓ canonicalizes case-only catalog model refs before local dispatch  529ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  109 passed (109)
   Start at  10:05:38
   Duration  8.07s (transform 2.66s, setup 439ms, import 4.69s, tests 2.68s, environment 0ms)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 14.53s
```

The aggregate budget prevents one `--file` invocation from allocating more than 500 MiB regardless of how many files are supplied. Sequential processing eliminates concurrent read amplification.

## Changes

- `src/cli/capability-cli/media-output.ts`: Add `MAX_TOTAL_CLI_INPUT_FILE_BYTES` (500 MiB), convert `readInputFiles` from `Promise.all` to sequential loop with budget tracking, pass budget through `readCliInputFileSafely`
